mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in WORKPLACES mobility reduces commuting-linked discretionary stops and suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. Because WORKPLACES has fallen from -28.0 to -36.6 in the latest snapshot, the retail channel should remain weaker unless workplace mobility stabilizes or rebounds.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES remains below its t-1w level for at least two more weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays above +20 percent for multiple weeks, people spend more time at home and shift purchases away from in-person retail, pushing RETAIL_REC down within two weeks. The current home-stay signal is persistent enough to keep retail visits compressed unless RESIDENTIAL drops back toward baseline.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +20 for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above +20 for two additional weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT combined with higher WORKPLACES mobility raises trip chaining and downtown foot traffic, which lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The mechanism requires both commuting and station activity to improve together; one without the other is not enough to change retail behavior materially.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior 28-day mean even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM falls sharply from an elevated level, short-run household errand traffic is being redirected away from essential shopping and into general retail, which can raise RETAIL_REC within one week. The effect is strongest when grocery activity drops after a spike rather than during stable demand.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls by more than 10 points week-on-week after being above +20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in the week after GROCERY_PHARM drops by more than 10 points from an elevated reading.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS mobility is a substitution signal for warm-weather leisure activity that also supports in-person shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC should edge up over the next four weeks. This mechanism needs outdoor activity to keep climbing rather than just one isolated week of park use.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its previous 28-day mean even while PARKS rises for three or more of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in RESIDENTIAL and fall in TRANSIT indicates a stay-at-home substitution away from travel-heavy outings, which depresses retail visits over the next two weeks. The mechanism fails if transit recovers quickly enough to offset the higher home-stay pattern.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and TRANSIT stays below its current weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in TRANSIT below the recent -40 range is a threshold signal that mobility restrictions or demand shocks are limiting shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC will weaken over the next four weeks. The retail effect should appear only after transit crosses that lower bound and not during ordinary fluctuations.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -40.3 in t-1w and -38.7 in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior 28-day mean after TRANSIT crosses below -40.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, a rebound in TRANSIT together with a recovery in PARKS signals broader mobility normalization that pulls people back into retail districts and raises RETAIL_REC over four weeks. The mechanism is specific to reopening because leisure and commuting trips reinforce each other there; it is not expected to operate under restriction tightening.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT and PARKS both improve from their current weekly means.
